title: Lesson 31 - Validation Rules and Error Messages in OmniScripts
description: Prescribe the implementation of robust validation rules, error messages, and conditional steps to guide users and manage unexpected outcomes or data inconsistencies.

questions.question: An OmniScript must ensure a phone number has at least 10 digits before the user advances. Where should this validation live?
options: At the element level, on the phone number field, firing as the user leaves it
At the step level, checking the whole step
questions.explanation: A single-field format check belongs at the element level, firing as the user leaves the field, which catches the error at the point of entry. Step-level validation is for cross-field checks, a Data Mapper transforms data, and a FlexCard displays it.

questions.question: A validation rule must check that a start date is before an end date, two fields in the same Step. Where should this validation live?
options: On the start date field, element level
At the step level, so both fields are present when it fires
On the end date field only
questions.explanation: A cross-field check needs both values present, so it belongs at the step level, which fires when the user tries to advance after both fields are entered. An element-level rule on one field fires before the other is entered and cannot see both values.

questions.question: A fetch stage in an OmniScript returns no data for a valid account. What is the correct error handling?
options: Read the status, show a clear message that no data was found, and log the details for diagnosis
Block the user with no message
Ignore it and continue with empty data
questions.explanation: Unexpected outcomes must surface in a way the user can act on: read the status, show a clear message, and log details for diagnosis. A generic message gives no guidance, blocking with no message traps the user, and ignoring it produces wrong results.
